note: Hand-curated. Detection is automated (Federal Register, court dockets, agency alerts) but assigning a modelling effect is a judgement call, so entries arrive as pull requests with an empty effect for a maintainer to fill. See PLAN.md 8.1. Every entry carries verified_against and confidence; the app must not display an entry whose last_checked is stale.

travel_ban_partial.note: Proclamation 10998, partial restrictions, added to the above for a combined 39.

iv_pause_75.note: INCOMPLETE. The full 75-country list was not captured during research; only a partial sample is recorded. Do not use this list to tell an individual they are unaffected. Resolve before the event layer gates any user-facing claim.

events.title: Stricter public charge standard for adjustment of status
events.summary: DHS rescinds the December 2022 public charge rule and replaces it with stricter sub-regulatory guidance and broad adjudicator discretion. A new Form I-485 keyed to the standard is issued the same day. Benefits received before the effective date are assessed under the old rule.

modeling.note: Direction is adverse for approval rates and adjudication speed, magnitude unknown. Leave null rather than invent a number; it widens the §6.5 approval curve rather than shifting it.

events.title: Immigrant visa interviews paused worldwide
events.summary: The State Department paused immigrant visa interviews at every post while consular officers complete public charge training. Adjustment of status at USCIS is not affected.

modeling.note: Unused EMPLOYMENT numbers stranded this way are lost at year end, not recycled. Unused FAMILY numbers do raise the next year's employment limit. See PLAN.md 1.5.

events.title: EB-4 non-minister religious worker category sunsets
events.summary: H.R. 7148, signed 3 February 2026, extended the non-minister special immigrant religious worker program only through 30 September 2026. No enacted further extension was found.

events.title: Travel ban, Proclamation 10949
events.summary: Entry restrictions on nationals of nineteen countries. Applies to entry from abroad; it does not by itself stop an adjustment of status case filed inside the United States.

events.title: Travel ban expansion, Proclamation 10998
events.summary: Partial restrictions added for twenty further countries, bringing the combined total to thirty-nine.

events.title: USCIS adjudication pause for travel-ban nationals
events.summary: Paused adjustment of status, work permit and advance parole adjudications for nationals of the listed countries. Began December 2025 for nineteen countries, expanded 1 January 2026 to thirty-nine, and was vacated by the District of Rhode Island on 5 June 2026. The underlying entry bans were not disturbed.

events.title: Immigrant visa issuance pause, 75 countries
events.summary: The State Department paused immigrant visa issuance for nationals of seventy-five countries on public charge grounds. A federal court held it unlawful and it ended on 21 August 2026.

modeling.note: Demand suppressed by a country-specific pause does not evaporate. The Visa Office reallocated the numbers by advancing other countries' cutoffs, and the affected countries rebound afterwards.

events.title: H-1B $100,000 fee proclamation
events.summary: A fee on H-1B petitions for beneficiaries abroad. Vacated at district court with the government's appeal pending. Affects the multi-year pipeline feeding future priority dates, not any current queue position.

events.title: Wage-weighted H-1B selection
events.summary: Cap-subject H-1B registrations are selected with weighting by wage level. Registrations fell from about 344,000 to about 210,000 year on year, which reduces the pipeline feeding priority dates several years out.

events.title: Gold Card draws on EB-1 and EB-2 numbers
events.summary: A pay-for-priority route drawing visa numbers from the existing EB-1 and EB-2 pools without changing the statutory caps. Uptake has been negligible: a few hundred requests and one approval by mid-2026, with litigation pending.

modeling.note: Negligible at observed uptake. Revisit if approvals reach the thousands.

events.title: Per-country cap reform: EAGLE Act and IVES Act (118th Congress)
events.summary: S.3291 and H.R.6542, which would have phased out the seven percent per-country limit for employment-based green cards. Died with the 118th Congress on 3 January 2025 without passing either chamber. A bill does not carry over between Congresses; reintroduction under new bill numbers would need its own entry once one is confirmed, not a revival of this one.

modeling.note: Structural. Would be modelled as a scenario in Level C, not applied to the base estimate. Kept in the registry, not deleted, so the card's exclusion logic has a real dead entry to be tested against.
